Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory

💡 Key Takeaways

  • At least three people have been killed after a fire at a confectionery factory in western Java on Saturday, with the death toll expected to rise.
  • Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for around 36 missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: Drone footage shows aftermath of deadly fire at Indonesian factory.

At least three people have been killed after a fire at a confectionery factory in western Java on Saturday, with the death toll expected to rise.

Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for around 36 missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.

Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries.

Rescuers recovered 24 body bags from the fire as of Sunday evening, as search operations continue to locate missing people.

Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire on Saturday evening.

The factory is in Serang district, Banten province, about 50km (31km) west of Jakarta. Authorities have not yet determined the fire's cause.

Photos and footage of the scene indicated the large factory taken over by flames during the night, firefighters battling the flames, and first responders retrieving at least one body from the wreckage on Sunday morning.

Local media reported that the search had been called off for the night late on Sunday, and would resume on Monday.

"All members of the joint SAR team are making every effort to locate the missing victims while prioritising the safety of personnel on the ground," the rescue agency remarked.

Relatives of the missing workers had gathered outside the factory waiting for updates, according to local broadcasts cited by AFP.

Firefighters had been called to the building at 16:30 local time (09:30 GMT) on Saturday - but it was already engulfed in flames, broadcaster Kompas TV reported, citing fire official Tubugas Machfudz.

"When we arrived (on location)... a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the firm's protection system was functioning properly or not," he said.

The factory is owned by PT Fonusa Agung Mulia, according to search and rescue authorities.

On LinkedIn the manufacturer describes itself as a subsidiary of UNIFAM, one of Indonesia's largest food and beverage companies.

#115916. Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2608 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.
  • You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf.
  • While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.

While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.

Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

Ask Proxy’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the tech giant explains on its website.

It has been revealed that it works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add vital dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.

Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a fresh activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy.

There’s also a work-focused version, which the firm explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.”.

Industry observers note that the personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees.

Ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625.

It has been revealed that caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone people and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.

Industry observers note that for instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026.

Sources indicate that comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished.

Sources indicate that completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies customers and recommends the next steps.

It can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. Comma maintains context and memory across devices and conversations, and can deliver daily briefings, flag urgent matters, and summarize recorded calls.

Comma is free to start and open source.

Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized initiative.

Industry observers note that the service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar.

Fambot presently connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with support for Apple Calendar planned for the future.

In a recent development, the organization rolled out in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is presently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription.

Folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations.

Sources indicate that one distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally.

Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background.

Haven distinguishes itself by presenting the concept of a “digital twin” rather than merely serving as a text-based AI assistant.

According to the company, Haven understands and adapts to your preferences, routines, and decision-making styles, creating a personalized memory graph based on your interactions. As the company describes, “A personal assistant knows what you asked it to do. Haven knows what you would do and how you would do it.”.

Notably, the company envisions future features that customize your experiences across devices, like TV and car.

Industry observers note that at the moment, Haven is available for free in beta on iPhone and Android devices, and the web. You can also reach Haven by calling or texting (435) 260-6500.

Instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion, valuing it at $10 billion.

The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. Consumers can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The manufacturer indicates early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and canceling subscriptions.

The firm remains in private beta.

Powered by Hermes Agent, Iris is designed to let owners delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request.

Martin is a general-purpose personal assistant reachable through SMS as well as phone, WhatsApp, email, Slack, and its own iOS app.

It can help manage calendars, email, reminders, tasks, notes, and communications. It can also act on behalf of consumers by sending messages or making phone calls, while providing daily summaries of what needs attention.

It’s a bit on the pricier side, with subscriptions starting at $21 per month.

Maverick describes itself as an “AI companion who lives in your texts,” acting as a personal assistant that helps manage everyday tasks directly from your messages.

It can fix typos, cancel subscriptions, schedule meetings from voice notes, and help group chats settle on a date for an event. One notable feature is that Maverick asks for your permission before taking action.

The platform also offers hundreds of integrations, including Discord, Gmail, and Slack, allowing it to connect with the apps you already use.

Industry observers note that it’s right now in beta and free to use on iMessage. There’s also a Pro version for €27 per month (or approximately $30.25 USD), which includes 500 tasks a month,  20 connected apps, scheduled tasks, and memory.

Miso takes the personal-assistant concept and applies it specifically to travel.

Recent findings suggest that it operates through iMessage and combines AI trip planning with support from a dedicated travel team. Users can arrange flights through messaging while Miso takes into account their travel preferences, loyalty points, and other priorities. Miso also gives travelers access to trip details and flight updates, along with personalized recommendations.

Ohai is another family assistant focused on helping households manage the constant stream of information and tasks involved in everyday family life.

Industry observers note that owners can send messages, forward emails, or make voice requests, and the assistant can transform them into schedules, reminders, and prepares. It can also coordinate calendars, household chores, and meals across multiple members of a family.

It includes a free basic option, but also offers different subscriptions based on family size, starting at $9.99 per month.

Orbits also has an AI assistant that is focused on the household.

It works through both the Orbits app and text messaging, and can bring together calendars, lists, and conversations while also carrying out tasks for you. That can include searching the web, making purchases, booking restaurants, changing appointments, and requesting quotes for household services.

Additionally, Orbits can remind family members about chores, communicate with service providers, and help coordinate responsibilities beyond the immediate household.

Orbits is backed by investors like Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Speedrun fund, N49P, and Garage Capital.

Sources indicate that users can interact with Pally as they would with a friend while giving it access to the apps they already rely on. The assistant can connect information spread across services such as WhatsApp, Gmail, calendars, and Google Drive, helping users keep track of plans, receipts, dates, files, and other details.

There’s a free plan available. It works over iMessage, RCS, and Telegram.

According to recent reports, poke introduced in March 2026 as a general-purpose assistant that you can reach through text messaging. It can handle tasks involving calendars, planning, health and fitness, smart-home controls, photos, and other everyday activities.

Poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform. A month later, parent organization The Interaction Company of California was acquired by AI coding startup Cognition in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

Rene is an AI personal assistant designed to be a user’s “best contact” rather than another productivity agent. It’s text-based and can turn natural-language conversations into tasks, reminders, summaries, and other follow-up actions. Rene also maintains context across conversations, allowing it to remember details and surface things that may need attention later.

Additionally, it has a browser, can write code, shop for you, as well as create slides and images.

Rene is at the moment available on iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Instead of waiting for customers to open an app, Skye is an “agentic homescreen” for the iPhone that analyzes information from connected services and surfaces what it thinks is relevant through contextual cards, suggestions, and daily briefings. The assistant can generate audio briefings, prepare information ahead of meetings, surface reminders, and identify potentially useful information.

Sources indicate that the manufacturer, Signull Labs, raised about $3.6 million in seed funding in 2025. It entered private testing and beta in April 2026, and hasn’t yet announced a public release date.

Recent findings suggest that stanley is an AI content assistant aimed at content creators rather than general personal productivity. Available through iMessage, Telegram, and the web, it acts as a kind of AI head of content, helping consumers come up with ideas, turn them into posts, and maintain a consistent publishing schedule.

For instance, Stanley can connect to a user’s Instagram account, using that context to suggest content based on what the user has actually been doing. Customers can also send voice notes, which Stanley turns into scripts, captions, and other social assets. It includes a content calendar and can schedule posts, with the broader goal of making content creation a more continuous, automated process rather than something users have to sit down and initiative from scratch.

It has been revealed that szn is designed to coordinate tasks and follow-ups through a single conversation thread. Consumers can send text messages, voice notes, photos, or forwarded emails, and the assistant takes action on their behalf, including making calls, sending emails, and managing follow-ups.

According to the organization’s website, Szn has served more than 7,500 businesses across 16 countries, completed over 10,000 jobs, and handled 95 hours of calls.

Tab allows users to delegate everyday tasks through familiar messaging platforms. Users can send requests to the assistant via iMessage or WhatsApp, ranging from ordering groceries to finding birthday gifts, and Tab handles the process on their behalf.

The company emerged from stealth in early October with a valuation of $300 million. Its investors include SV Angel, Valar Ventures, and American Spirit.

The biggest differentiator with Tomo’s personal assistant for iMessage is that, instead of being a private assistant that only you interact with, Tomo can become part of group conversations.

Also, like other agents, it’s designed to help with goals, accountability, scheduling, and everyday organization. It also has the ability to send reminders, search the web, work with calendars and email, watch videos, and edit photos.

The basic plan starts at $19.99 per month.

Town is aimed more at professional life. It gives users a “Townie,” an AI assistant designed to learn how they work and handle recurring professional tasks. It can work with email, calendars, documents, Slack, and other platforms.

In June 2026, the tech giant raised a $55 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner.

Recent findings suggest that underdog is a privacy-focused AI assistant that introduced an invite-only beta in early October 2026. Unlike cloud-based AI services, the model runs entirely on the user’s device, keeping personal data on hardware they already own. The initial release supports Mac and Windows computers, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions planned for the future.

The tech giant looks to offer the app for free initially and has stated that it will never include advertising.

Wajo’s first consumer agent, Fo, can call businesses, send emails, join group chats, make bookings and purchases, and coordinate with people to complete everyday tasks.

A key part of Wajo’s approach is giving Fo its own identity. The agent has its own email address, phone number, and payment card, allowing it to interact with businesses without requiring users to hand over their own credentials.

Notably, when Fo encounters something it cannot handle on its own, Wajo indicates it can bring in a human assistant to finish the task.

Fo released publicly in September 2026 with a free tier, while heavier workloads and custom agents are available through a paid Pro offering.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Auracast broadcasts are an integral part of the storytelling in this off-Broadway show about love, connections, and hearing loss.

Auracast broadcasts are an integral part of the storytelling in this off-Broadway show about love, connections, and hearing loss.

Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse. As we filter to our seats, ushers hand each person a black drawstring bag with a pair of wired headphones connected to a small Auracast receiver. Then, soon after the play begins, we’re instructed to put them on.

The headphones are an integral storytelling tool of Love Me — a one-man show from the minds of stand-up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer Drew Michael and director Prashanth Venkataramanujam. It’s a show about love and the bid for connection, told in five chapters about different relationships in Michael’s life, bound by the threads of his hearing loss and self-discovery.

Sources indicate that love Me’s experimental sound design is possible thanks to Auracast, a technology based on Bluetooth that can broadcast a high-quality audio stream to any number of nearby devices. As the show follows Michael from childhood through adulthood, sound designer Daniel Kluger uses the headphones in combination with the theater speakers to create experiences that wouldn’t be possible with a traditional setup. Tinnitus ringing and hearing test tones play in the music between sections as subtle clues as the show builds to Michael’s epiphany about his hearing loss. Kluger also explores the world through varying levels of sonic clarity. Sound playing through the theater’s speakers is sometimes intentionally muffled, which is then further dulled by the headphones, giving the audience a sense of what Michael is hearing in those moments.

But one sound that stays clear and pristine is Michael’s inner monologue, heard in the headphones throughout the show. The inner monologue consists of both prerecorded tracks and the live feed from Michael’s microphone on stage as he talks back and forth with himself. “Any time you’re in my head — anything in the headphones is coming through clearly,” Michael tells me after the show. “[We’re] trying to also highlight that the appeal of the inner world is such that it’s the highest fidelity space for this person. It’s more comfortable.”.

Recent findings suggest that the different sound sources and treatments of the sound can lead to intentionally confusing scenes for the audience. During one, where Michael is doing a stand-up set at a comedy club, three sounds compete for attention: The theater speakers play the crowd’s reactions (including a heckler whose voice is sometimes muffled and sometimes clear); his prerecorded inner monologue reacting to the crowd plays in the headphones; and on stage, Michael is performing the set, with his mic muffled so our focus is on his inner monologue. It’s one of the definitive moments where the audience feels the constant concentration necessary to parse what’s happening when sounds aren’t clear and become overwhelming.

But the biggest impact comes during a climactic scene the sound design has been building toward, a realization that also incorporates the visuals of a series of Michael’s audiograms over the years. “I had this massive breakthrough about the whole history of what I’ve been doing — the cognitive labor, the invisible to myself labor that was affecting every single minute of my life,” Michael notes. “That was a huge moment.”.

According to recent reports, that’s when the audience is instructed to remove the headphones we’ve been wearing for nearly the entire show. As Michael comes to the recognition of his relationship with his hearing loss and the clarity of mind that gives him, what we’ve become used to for the entire show’s experience — the headphones — are now gone, as is that literal weight from our heads. It’s an emotional moment, one that I’ve thought about multiple times since seeing the show.

It also leads into the final act, where Michael begins to understand his own Deaf identity. “The deafness is not the culprit, it’s the denial of it.” he tells me. “My hearing presently has never been worse, but I’ve never been more self-affirmed or self-actualized or felt happier in myself. It’s a misconception, I think, about deafness as a tragedy, deafness as a deficit, deafness as a burden, deafness as something that plagues a person.”.

The ability of Auracast to broadcast an audio stream that any number of headphones can connect to is what made Love Me a possibility. Any Auracast headphones can connect to the audience broadcast — I brought along the Nothing Pro 1 to test the ability and connected to the audience broadcast channel in seconds — but I used the provided Auri receiver and Austrian Audio headset for the performance. The show’s sound was designed with those in mind, and I didn’t want the differing isolation of the Nothing headphones to affect the intent of the experience.

According to recent reports, love Me is presented in partnership with Deaf West Theatre, which supports Deaf-centered storytelling in theatrical productions. In addition to the audience Auracast feed, there’s one for users of hearing aids and cochlear implants that’s designed for compliance with those devices, and iPads with captions are also available. During the performance, Michael connects to his own broadcast channel with Auracast-enabled Phonak Eon Sphere hearing aids. “We talked about using in-ear monitors, but if I use an in-ear monitor, then I don’t have amplification from my environment, so then I lose contact with the audience,” Michael states. “These function as two things: They’re hearing aids and also in-ear monitors.”.

Love Me relies on the Auracast technology to tell its story, but it isn’t a story about hearing technology. The technology is there to tell the story of connection and discovery of identity. “I think right now … there are two things that are at odds — the hearing aid and audiological tech side of deafness and then the cultural identity side of deafness,” Michael claims. Technological improvements, like cochlear implants and hearing aids, are cited as one of the reasons schools for the deaf have been on the decline, which leads to kids being mainstreamed (put into regular public schools) and losing out on Deaf history and culture. “I’m not against the tech,” Michael says, “I just think tech and Deaf identity should be a marriage rather than a divide.”.

In a recent development, and that collaboration is why Love Me works as well as it does. The Auracast technology is there both for accessibility — in the same way it’s already used in other performances, lectures, or announcement systems — and to uplift the show’s story of love, acceptance, and acknowledgement of one’s own Deaf identity. It’s an inventive use of the technology that carries with it a powerful message.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam.

South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation.

He mentioned he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung.

In a recent development, A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone and AI tools. This prompted officials to act urgently to detect hidden devices, including sending emergency alerts to every single mobile phone in the country.

The Suneung takes up to nine hours to complete, and it plays a major role in career trajectories of millions of South Koreans.

South Korean high school pupils in Daegu check their answers, a day after the annual college entrance exam.

"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier stated 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

Concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

These fears came to a boil last weekend, when Han Won-seok, the top tax accountancy exam scorer in April, admitted to cheating.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," the 34-year-old noted in a video message.

This prompted the authorities to introduce urgent measures, with just days ahead of the Suneung.

This included sending nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea used its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told Yonhap he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

South Korea catches 111 students with new measures against exam cheating.

The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), according to reports in CNN and the Associated Press.

Sources indicate that the NCIC is the online database used by federal and local law enforcement to share information about warrants, background checks, and more. The scope of the breach does not yet appear to be clear.

A former FBI official told CNN that they’re not just concerned about “whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an problem, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.”.

In September, the FBI reportedly told agents and support staff that their personal information had been stolen in a cyberattack.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation.

A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad.

That changed last week, as Haitian police and troops from El Salvador reconquered the stadium. Nayib Bukele, El Salvador’s authoritarian president, called the development a step towards delivering Haiti from a criminal insurrection that has displaced more than 1.5 million people and killed thousands.

“We now have the upper hand on the ground,” claimed Bukele, who has sent more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti since mid-October.

Outside the Sylvio Cator stadium, named after an acclaimed Haitian athlete who won a silver medal at the 1928 Olympics, there were joyous scenes as citizens celebrated a foreign politician they hope will prove an unlikely saviour.

Sources indicate that “There’s a wind of hope blowing through our country and, thanks to God, we will get through this. Long live Bukele!” said a 55-year-old decorator who asked to be named as Bòs Baton.

Recent findings suggest that stood by Sanon’s battle-scarred fresco, Baton recalled being driven from an area called Poste-Marchand after criminals set his home ablaze during an armed uprising that started in February 2024. “Today, we are happy because there are places we couldn’t go to before that are accessible – and it’s thanks to Bukele’s intervention that we can be here today,” Baton said.

Identical sentiments have been voiced on the streets of El Salvador’s capital, San Salvador, in recent years as a result of Bukele’s controversial anti-gang crusade, which has freed millions from gang rule – albeit at a high price.

Since that crackdown began in early 2022, more than 90,000 Salvadorans have been jailed as part of a mass incarceration campaign that has slashed murder rates but also fuelled fears that El Salvador’s democracy has died.

Bukele’s domestic clampdown has made the millennial strongman a darling for rightwing politicians and voters across Latin America and the Caribbean, who hold his actions up as proof that, with an iron fist and a malleable approach to human rights, rampant criminality can be tamed.

Now, as Bukele seeks to extend his seven-year presidency in an election in February, he is hoping to burnish his gang-busting credentials overseas.

“It’s an operation that projects force, that projects Bukele’s image as the saviour … and positions El Salvador as a key reference in the region for [how] … to deal with gangs and security,” noted Tiziano Breda, a Latin America regional expert from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project.

Industry observers note that the extent of Bukele’s ambitions in Haiti is unclear. The operation’s trigger was the 18 October abduction of four Salvadoran aviation technicians who worked for a UN-backed security force. On Monday, Bukele’s vice-president, Félix Ulloa, revealed Salvadoran troops would withdraw as soon as the four men were rescued, “because this is not an occupying force – we are not there to stay”.

But Ulloa also noted his government was responding altruistically “to a cry for help from the Haitian people and government”, suggesting its mission could be extended.

Sources indicate that bukele has also hinted his plans go beyond short-lived ground operations to recover his citizens, or their remains. “We will triumph. God will give us victory,” the politician vowed this week.

Many Haitians hope his combatants will stay and have been thrilled by cinematic social media clips posted by Bukele showing helicopter strikes on a gang compound and the mansion of a gangster nicknamed Taliban.

In a recent development, banners and billboards around Port-au-Prince celebrate Bukele as a 21st-century liberator and feature slogans such as “The bandits won’t get a wink of sleep!” and “We’re tired! Give us Bukele!”.

Standing outside the liberated football ground, bricklayer Venel Saindor recalled how criminals torched his home in Carrefour-Feuilles three years ago. “It’s impossible to enter my neighbourhood because the thieves are still there. They shoot at us,” the 56-year-old explained, lifting his shirt to reveal a bullet scar above his right nipple.

“We need Bukele to help us return to our homes,” added Saindor, as a Salvadoran soldier with a belt-fed heavy machine gun kept watch from the stadium’s terraces.

Monique Clesca, a writer and activist, echoed the bricklayer’s enthusiasm. “Haitians are elated … [and] I feel elated also … It is a moment of hope,” she remarked on Tuesday, as thousands of demonstrators poured on to the streets to champion Bukele, chanting: “Viv Bukele!” and “Bukele is not playing games!”.

As a sea of protesters swept towards the prime minister’s offices, people from all walks of life spoke of how armed groups had destroyed their lives and their collective hope that Bukele may provide a solution.

“I used to drive an old bus. The bandits burned it. They burned my house down too,” said Wilné Persona, a 50-year-old driver, adding: “Bukele is the one we are waiting for … because we can no longer bear the situation.”.

A food vendor called Claudy Mayas urged “Papa Bukele” to stand his ground. “Bukele, I bless you, your wife and your children,” noted Mayas, 51. “The Haitian people are with you, just as you are with us.”.

Recent findings suggest that clesca attributed the palpable excitement to the widespread perception that Bukele’s “decisive” action had exposed the incompetence, inefficiency and indifference of Haitian and foreign leaders. “Basically, what Bukele has done is show that leadership is about resolving a problem for your population,” she stated, praising how the stadium and other areas were recaptured in less than a month.

Amid the excitement there is also unease. Some fear Bukele’s offensive could exacerbate an already volatile situation in and around Haiti’s capital, much of which resembles a war zone. This week, there was heavy fighting between Salvadoran troops, police and gangs in Village of God, the shantytown that is Izo’s main base. On Thursday, police remarked officers had killed at least 34 suspected criminals during an operation near the stadium.

In a recent development, some suspect El Salvador’s president, a social media whiz with 22 million followers on X and TikTok, could be exaggerating his troops’ role in recent successes with help from a strike team of online propagandists and fans. “Nayib Bukele is gang kryptonite,” one US enthusiast gushed this week, calling his intervention “a miracle”.

Others fret over Bukele’s ability to distinguish between gang members and civilians, given the indiscriminate nature of his mass detention campaign in El Salvador, where thousands of innocent people have been jailed without due process.

Clesca downplayed concerns over the toll Bukele’s crackdown has taken on democracy and the rule of law in El Salvador, which now has the world’s highest per capita incarceration rate. Haitian politics was so contaminated with organised crime, she argued, “it’s almost like the mafia has taken over 10 Downing Street”.

“If you’re talking about [an] assault on democracy, Haiti is … almost a case study that is … even worse, more flagrant, than El Salvador,” Clesca stated.

The security situation was so dire that urgent action was needed. “Let’s just be honest … in Haiti, we’re being brutalised,” Clesca said. “Girls are being taken as sexual slaves. They’re being gang raped. So somewhere along the line, we have to say: ‘Haiti helped [South American independence hero] Simón Bolívar [who received shelter and support from Haiti in the early 1800s] … and now, Bukele is helping us’.”.

At Tuesday’s rally, protesters spoke of El Salvador’s president in divine terms. “Today, we see Bukele as a saviour, as someone sent by God,” remarked one man, before adding a word of caution that spoke to countless past interventions that have ended in frustration and failure.

It has been revealed that “There is one thing I will say to President Bukele,” he noted. “He must not start with us and leave us halfway.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, as I wrote previously, Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One, setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki’s sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most.

Industry observers note that (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We’ll give you a heads-up when we get there.).

According to recent reports, as I wrote previously, Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One, setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945.

Knocked unconscious, Kōichi survived and awoke to find his parents and many others were killed in the World War II bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and the orphaned baby she rescued, Akiko (Sae Nagatani). But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island. Kōichi saved the day and lived to tell the tale. He reunited with Noriko, who had a strange black bruise on her neck. And we saw a chunk of Godzilla’s remains start to regenerate, leaving things open for a sequel.

Godzilla Minus One was a massive hit, both in Japan—where it remains one of the highest grossing Japanese films ever—and worldwide, racking up $116 million globally and winning an Oscar for best visual effects. Yamazaki stated in interviews at the time that there had as yet been no talk of a sequel—while also hinting at future directions a sequel might explore. He later admitted it was way of planting a seed for what would become Godzilla Minus Zero.

Godzilla Minus Zero is set two years after the events of the first film, with Kamiki and Hamabe reprising their roles as Kōichi and Noriko, along with Nagatani as Akiko. The family is just trying to live in peace after the devastation Godzilla inflicted on their country. Alas, a new kaiju emerges, arriving via meteorite and using its tentacles to feed on local wildlife before morphing into a dragon-like creature that causes fresh rampaging destruction. Fans of the genre will recognize this creature as Ghidorah, whose appearance in the film was teased in the various trailers.

It isn’t long before Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka)—i.e., the dude with the magnificent wavy gray hair who is director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau—seeks out Kōichi for help in dealing with this new kaiju threat. His team is able to track Ghidorah’s movements via electrical storms and other pertinent weather patterns, thanks to meteorologist Makoto Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa). But the team has no idea how they might defeat this new threat to life and infrastructure. It’s hardly a spoiler to note that at some point, a regenerated Godzilla will come into play.

(WARNING: significant spoilers appear below. Stop reading now if you haven’t seen the film.).

Industry observers note that yamazaki has retained the visual tone that made the film’s predecessor so striking; it feels like classic Godzilla fare of yore, just with 21st century cutting-edge visual effects. If anything, he’s upped his game on the special effects front, reflecting the larger production budget he had to work with. (It’s also the first Japanese movie filmed specifically for IMAX and it’s well-worth seeing in that format.).

Much of that budget went toward bringing the central monsters to cinematic life, and Godzilla Minus Zero does not disappoint. Ghidorah, for instance, responds to a bombing attack by mutating into its famous three-headed King Ghidorah form, complete with a spiffy fresh superpower: a “gravity beam” that lets the creature levitate entire houses (and, at one point, Godzilla) into the sky before dropping them back to the ground. And the kaiju vs. kaiju battle is spectacular in both scope and execution.

Industry observers note that yamazaki even managed to squeeze in what he called his “bucket-list” special effects shot inspired by a scene in 2008’s Cloverfield: Godzilla looming out of the Atlantic Ocean in front of the Statue of Liberty to wreck havoc on the statue and Upcoming York City in general. Granted, it occurs in a dream sequence of biologist Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), who survived the Hiroshima blast that killed his wife and children and longs for revenge. And it’s not just indulgence on the director’s part: the scene reinforces the traditional theme of linking Godzilla to nuclear radiation and the horrors of the atomic bomb.

Nor does Yamazaki ignore the human factor via the dilemma of his nuclear family trio. Kōichi must wrestle with his conscience: how can he risk his life again to battle a kaiju when it could mean leaving Akiko an orphan yet again should he fail? Noriko is infected with Godzilla’s radioactive G-cells—the only human to survive the mutations in her own body for so long. But her time could be running out, plus they’ve kept her infection secret for fear she will be taken away by the government for experimentation. Sometimes doing the right thing comes at great personal cost, and watching these quite ordinary people grapple with that reality brings emotional depth to the film.

It has been revealed that the film ends on a suitably bittersweet note, and while Yamazaki hasn’t dropped any hints about a possible third film in the series, we’d love to learn more about Noriko’s strangely symbiotic connection to Godzilla via the G-cells in her bloodstream. Long may he reign.

Godzilla Minus Zero is still playing in theaters.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Several thousand people in Istanbul took to the streets on Sunday to protest the closure of several opposition-linked media outlets in Turkey.

Protesters chanted, cheered, and whistled as they marched several kilometers through the city, calling for press freedom and freedom of expression.

They carried a huge banner that read: "We want freedom of thought, freedom of the press, and freedom for journalists." The protesters were also carrying placards that read, "The press cannot be silenced.".

Turkey's main opposition party, Yeni Parti, called for a protest just days after police raided Sozcu TV, one of the last opposition-aligned television channels.

Recent findings suggest that senior staff members were arrested during the raid. A government-appointed trustee was installed, and the TV tech giant was placed under compulsory administration.

It was the third takeover in a year following similar actions against Tele1, Halk TV, Turkey's most-watched news channel, and the leading digital news website, T24.

Timur Soykan, a journalist who was briefly detained for criticizing the government, remarked that the government was doing everything in its power to silence journalists but was failing to do so.

Soykan asked the public to support Halk TV journalists, who proposal to continue broadcasting on a newly introduced YouTube channel.

Over the past decade, press freedom has faced sustained pressure in the form of prosecutions, digital censorship, and government accusations that journalists are spreading "fake news.".

In a recent development, in the last two months alone, Turkey has arrested several journalists for their reporting on a multibillion-dollar investment fund scandal. At least two of the journalists remain in pretrial detention.

According to the media rights group MLSA, twenty-five journalists are currently imprisoned in Turkey.

This year, Reporters Without Borders ranked Turkey 163rd out of 180 countries in its Press Freedom Index.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no looks for Huang to return.
  • Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the tech giant’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the manufacturer’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no looks for Huang to return.

Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the tech giant’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.).

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Industry observers note that kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.

What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.

A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and stated, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.

Tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country.

Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China.

And again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line.

Sources indicate that kirsten: Although Nvidia’s bottom line is doing just fine. In every possible way, their guidance was incredible. They beat expectations. They have a long pipeline.

It was really interesting because you have that happening, and then you have all this noise happening in social media, and also a number of other tech conferences were happening this past week — Dealbook Summit, there [were] a few others in which you had the highest profile people that you can think of in the tech world commenting on Jensen [Huang], and Jensen himself commenting.

So it’s like the tale of two Nvidias this week. You’ve got the earnings and the current executives really talking about, “Hey, we’ve got this.” In fact, that was the last line that Collette Kress remarked [on the earnings call]. And then at the exact same time, or in parallel, you’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back. So it’s really quite the drama that we are definitely not done with, by the way.

Recent findings suggest that anthony: Although I think that what the folks who’d like to see Jensen Huang come back would say is that this most recent quarter is the last quarter under him. This is the [last of the] good times that we’re seeing under him. And so we don’t know how well Nvidia will do without him.

It seems like Nvidia’s public stance right now [on Huang’s possible return] is, “No, that’s not happening.” But Nvidia’s public stance a week and a half before that was, “We stand behind Jensen. We have every confidence in his leadership.”.

Recent findings suggest that so depending on the various pressures on them, you can imagine that changing. I don’t know what it would take for that to happen. I don’t necessarily think it’s that likely, but I also don’t think that just because they’re saying it’s not happening now doesn’t mean it will never happen.

Kirsten:  Sure, never say never.

Tim: Right, never say never. I do think that to some extent, their steadfastness and how quickly they shot down the petitions asking for Jensen to return suggests there’s maybe a little bit more going on behind the scenes than we know on the outside. So that’s probably something to watch in the coming weeks.

Kirsten: I think that the board is trying to be in control here, and they don’t want to be forced into a decision because someone like Elon Musk is saying that it needs to happen. And so, even if there is a day in which Jensen returns — which I think is pretty unlikely, especially because the investigation into how much and who knew what about chips being sold, allegedly, secretly to China. We don’t know the full picture of that yet. But even if they did have the full picture, they want to present control, and they definitely don’t want to appear like they have deference to some other tech billionaire out there.

Tim: I’m sure they’re looking at what happened at OpenAI and not wanting to repeat that.

Industry observers note that anthony: I imagine the dynamic’s a little bit different, since Nvidia is a public company. So, I’m not an expert on this, but I would guess it would be much harder for you Jensen Huang to come back and just toss out a bunch of board members.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finland says work is continuing on the Sparta II ship on Sunday.

A Russian cargo vessel that was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland is being towed away, authorities have said.

The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, sparking a fire aboard.

It then drifted into Finnish waters and its crew were evacuated to Russia. Finnish defence forces stated Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday afternoon that fire was no longer visible from the outside but thermal cameras highlighted that some containers on the ship were still warm.

The Sparta II was "slightly listing", Finnish authorities added, but the "situation is stable" and no fuel or other "hazardous substance leaks" had been detected.

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones appeared to have been used in the strike and that there was "no threat" to his territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian tech giant, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company claims it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard noted it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials remarked.

Industry observers note that "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo remarked. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.".

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry stated a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

While Besprozvannykh initially remarked the crew of the Sparta II intended to repair the ship and carry on their journey, the Finnish Border Guard later said they had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was en route to Russia.

Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, director of maritime operations at the Finnish Border Guard, mentioned during a news conference on Sunday that one Sparta II crew member had suffered minor injuries.

The Russian rescue vessel Murman is leading towing operations with the support of a Finnish guard ship and a Estonian naval patrol vessel.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

Finnish Defence Minister Antti HÃ¤kkÃ¤nen said that the Border Guard was responsible for the investigation into the attack and was co-operating with other relevant authorities.

Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry stated.

According to recent reports, the Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.

Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland.

  • The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.
  • Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade.

The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

The alleged leader of a major drug-trafficking cartel, the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO), he had managed to evade arrest for more than a decade, even though there was a reward of up to $5m (£3.8m) on his head.

His FBI “most wanted” poster states his organisation “is allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution and importation of large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States, and has predominately controlled drug production, transportation and distribution in several locations throughout Mexico”.

Mexico’s defence ministry also alleged he is the leader of the Beltrán Leyva criminal organisation, which is allied to the Mayos, one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel.

Meza Flores’s alleged second-in-command, Germán N, whose alias is “Serafín”, and José N, an alleged financial operator for the Beltrán Leyva group, were also arrested.

The operation to capture the men was carried out by “elite military forces” with help from US intelligence, according to Mexico’s defence ministry.

After arriving in the “target area … using stealth and surprise”, the ministry noted the arresting force came under attack “with gunfire and explosives” but managed to enter a house and make the arrests.

The men were then evacuated to Mexico City on a Mexican air force plane to be handed over to prosecutors.

Videos and photos show civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game at Kuroda Park stadium in Guasave, as well as burnt-out cars.

A barrage of rapid fire from what appeared to be Mexican security force helicopters hit the ground, according to CNN, and players from the Venados de Mazatlán and Algodoneros de Guasave teams abandoned the field mid-game.

Four Mexican army infantry soldiers died in the operation, the defence ministry remarked in a statement posted on X that extended the institution’s condolences to their families.

It added that security forces killed seven attackers and arrested eight alleged criminals in the operation, including three who were transferred to Mexico City and five who were turned over to the attorney general’s office in Culiacán, Sinaloa.

Overnight on Friday the ​military operation triggered a wave of violence in the state of Sinaloa, including armed ‌clashes between Mexican security forces and cartel members, who ‌set up flaming roadblocks in some areas.

By ​Saturday the violence had substantially subsided. Sinaloa state authorities ​said “the situation is under control and being addressed by all levels of government”.

Meza Flores was originally indicted in 2012, and in 2013 the US Treasury placed sanctions on him under the Kingpin Act, freezing his assets.

In 2017, the US Department of State’s Narcotics Rewards Program began offering up to $5m as a reward for information leading directly to his arrest or conviction.

He has been charged with multiple counts of drug-trafficking violations, and use and possession of a firearm in the US, and was wanted in Mexico for organised crime and offences against public health.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Signal declared Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”.

“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she noted. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Firm helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people.
  • Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds.
  • British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Firm helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people.

Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds.

British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.

Sources indicate that in the 1840s, Cuba was the most vital foreign source of copper ore for the UK. Copper was critical to Manchester’s cotton industry, railways and telegraphy.

Previous research has revealed that dozens of financiers involved in the founding in 1694 of the Bank of England invested in enslavement.

Now, Evans’s research reveals that ties between key figures in the UK’s financial system and enslavement of African peoples continued even after the government outlawed it.

Britain abolished its trade in enslaved people in 1807 and passed legislation abolishing slavery in most of its empire in 1833.

However, as Britain’s Slavery Abolition Act was coming into force, “City of London figures” were developing mining of El Cobre’s copper ore deposits, an operation which depended on enslavement in Spanish-controlled Cuba.

Key players in the highly lucrative operation included the Bank of England directors Charles Pascoe Grenfell (1790-1867) and William Thompson (1792-1854), acting in a private capacity.

Enslaved copper miners at El Cobre were likely to have been trafficked to Cuba by illegal voyages from the Bight of Biafra, in modern-day Nigeria, as Evans details in his book, Slavery’s Long Goodbye – Capitalism, Nationalism and Christianity in the Age of British Emancipation.

The death rate at El Cobre means it is likely that thousands of Africans were exploited there. Their life stories remain largely undocumented. At the time, slavery was legal in Cuba but the importation of enslaved people was not.

As a partner in the Cobre mining and export firm, Grenfell was a driving force in enslaved miners’ exploitation.

Cobre was “likely to be the largest slave enterprise in the western hemisphere” by the 1840s, Evans remarked. Investors who held Cobre shares from the outset received £102 in dividends for every £40 share between 1836 and 1865.

Grenfell was also a partner in a Swansea-based smelter Pascoe, Grenfell & Sons, which bought imports from the mine, in an era when the Welsh port was the centre of the global copper trade.

Meanwhile, Thompson, a former lord mayor of London, exploited enslaved miners through the ore export firm he directed, the Royal Santiago Organization.

The UK is facing increased pressure to make a formal apology to Caribbean and African nations for Britain’s centuries-long perpetuation of transatlantic chattel slavery. Commonwealth leaders say “structured dialogue” with the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, will begin in the next year.

While the Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has claimed Britain has nothing to apologise for, scholarship – dating back to the Trinidadian statesman Eric Williams’s 1944 book, Capitalism and Slavery – reveals the global impact of the colonialism and chattel enslavement that was integral to British capitalism’s success.

Evans, a former professor at the University of South Wales, said: “As Britain ostentatiously winds down its own slave system in the 1830s, British capital is boosting slavery elsewhere in the western hemisphere.

According to recent reports, “The illegal trade, involving French and Spanish merchants, was flourishing and substantial. There were British (anti-slavery) patrols off the coast of Cuba, but they’re relatively few in number and intercept only a very small proportion of slave ships.”.

According to recent reports, conditions at El Cobre were “extremely brutal”, with daily violence and torture. “Slave catchers” were employed to snatch miners who tried to escape to the mountains.

According to recent reports, in 1817, under British pressure, Spanish authorities signed a treaty that banned trafficking enslaved Africans to Cuba. But as Cuba’s sugar and coffee plantations relied on enslaved African workers, local colonial authorities ignored it, with 25,000 captives arriving in 1859 alone.

In 1843, pressure from the British and Foreign Anti-Slavery Society prompted legislation intended to prohibit British subjects from owning enslaved people in other jurisdictions, after undercover investigations exposed British mining companies’ activities in Brazil and Cuba, including at El Cobre.

Industry observers note that but after lobbying by mining interests, parliament diluted the legislation, allowing companies to retain enslaved workers as their “property” and hire others. The concessions prompted abolitionists to withdraw their support for the law, which failed to end the exploitation.

Neither Grenfell nor Thompson appears to have faced legal penalties for their involvement. Grenfell became the Liberal MP for Preston in the late 1840s, later boasting that his father had been an abolitionist. Grenfell remained a B of E director until 1864.

In a recent development, enslavement at El Cobre finally ended after Cuban revolutionaries captured the town from Spanish forces in November 1868. The rebel commander proclaimed the miners’ emancipation on Upcoming Year’s Eve, and formerly enslaved workers later joined Cuba’s liberation army.

Evans’s book explores Britain’s overlapping histories of slavery, capitalism and missionary Christianity through the lives of Grenfell and two of his cousins.

Evans added: “The British in the early 19th century had started to understand slavery as a national sin.

“In the classical age of abolition, you could do things like abstain from eating sugar from the West Indies.

“But with copper, you can’t do that because it’s embodied in the industrial world, and, in the age of joint-stock capitalism, you have many British people who invest in mining companies who genuinely didn’t know these companies were using enslaved workers.

According to recent reports, “Slavery was rendered invisible by the complexity of industrial society. But British engagement with slavery continued long after Emancipation. It involved the mercantile-financial elite of London as well as hundreds, possibly thousands, of rank-and-file investors from the Victorian middle class.”.

A Bank of England spokesperson noted: “We have previously acknowledged the role of former governors and directors in the slave trade.”.

GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them.
  • The global food system is ultimately driven by demand.
  • With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our latest research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land.

The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access.

With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses.

In a recent development, the biggest effects, however, occurred when reduced calorie intake was combined with a shift toward healthier diets. In this scenario, up to 7 million deaths could be avoided each year by 2050, while around 46 million hectares of agricultural land would have become available for other uses. This suggests that alongside weight-loss medicines, we need to make healthier options more widely available, affordable, and more appealing.

It has been revealed that food systems are interconnected across countries. If demand falls in one part of the world, this can affect farming, trade, and food prices elsewhere, with consequences for people who are not taking the medications at all.

Lower demand from GLP-1 users, for instance, could make food cheaper. That sounds positive, but cheaper food could also encourage greater consumption among non-users, offsetting some of the intended benefit. The effects of widespread GLP-1 use, in other words, cannot be understood just by looking at individual patients’ weight loss. They ripple through the global food system.

It’s tempting to read these findings as an argument for putting more people on weight-loss medication. That would miss the bigger picture.

Obesity has often been framed as a “lifestyle disease,” blaming individual people for not having enough willpower. But diets are shaped by what food is available, what it costs, how it’s marketed, where shops are located, and what’s most convenient. In many high-income countries, it is remarkably easy to consume large amounts of cheap, energy-dense food. Society tells people to make healthier choices while surrounding them with an environment that often encourages the opposite.

The UK government-commissioned national food strategy, finalized in 2021, made this point clearly: improving diets can’t simply be about asking individuals to choose better. The wider food environment needs to change to make the better choice the easy one.

Our findings shouldn’t be taken to mean that people living with obesity have a responsibility to lose weight to reduce the environmental impacts of food production. Rather, our research examines the wider consequences that changes in food demand could have across the food system.

A healthier diet is not necessarily just a diet with fewer calories. It could mean more fruit, vegetables, and other nutritious foods, alongside less excessive consumption of foods linked to poor health. These changes affect not only human health but also agriculture, land use, and the environment.

According to recent reports, rather than asking whether GLP-1 medications or healthier diets are the answer, let’s ask how they can work together. Imagine a food system where healthier foods are affordable and accessible, unhealthy options aren’t relentlessly promoted, agricultural policy supports nutritious and sustainable production, and people who need medical treatment can access it. That combination could be far more powerful than any single intervention.

In a recent development, GLP-1 medicines can play an key role in tackling obesity, but they shouldn’t become a technological fix that allows the wider food system to escape scrutiny. They can help people eat less in an unhealthy food environment, but the long-term goal should be to make it easier and more affordable to have a healthier, more sustainable diet.

The remarkable thing about GLP-1 medications may not be that they change how much food people eat. It may be that they show us, with new clarity, just how closely human health, food production, and environmental health are connected, and how much could be gained if we tackled all three together.

Roslyn Henry is Lecturer, School of Biological Sciences, University of Aberdeen and Peter Alexander is Professor of Global Food Systems, University of Edinburgh.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debut LP from Sheherazaad blends traditional Indian instruments with Western electronic flourishes and feminist narratives.

The debut LP from Sheherazaad blends traditional Indian instruments with Western electronic flourishes and feminist narratives.

Sheherazaad started making ripples in the music world a few years ago with her EP Qasr, which was produced by Grammy Award winner Arooj Aftab. Now she’s back with Khudgarzi, her reverb-drenched folk-noir debut LP that’s primarily sung in Urdu.

According to recent reports, the instrumentation on Khudgarzi draws on traditional South Asian music, including Carnatic and Hindustani styles, but also dabbles in Arabic folk traditions, as well as modern Western electronic music. Trip-hop flourishes and Spaghetti Western guitar brush up against tanbur and ghatam. Sheherazaad’s stunning voice sits atop dripping percussion and seasick drones singing about the plight of “The Selfish Woman.”.

Sources indicate that for Sheherazaad, the character of the selfish woman isn’t the villain, it’s a charge leveled at women who didn’t conform to societal norms, “eccentric women whose desire for agency was often met with an awful end.” Even if you can’t understand most of the lyrics, the atmosphere tells the story clearly enough. From the barely simmering anger of “Registaan” to the bleak repetition of “Qatil” and the fantastical yearning of “Zeher,” Khudgarzi is clearly the work of a woman exploring what it means to be a woman, the lasting legacy of colonialism, and the perpetual threats of a patriarchal society.

Khudgarzi is alternately a funeral dirge and a celebration of femininity. Sheherazaad owes a lot of the album’s ability to navigate these various themes and moods to her impressive production work, top-notch mixing by J. Valleau, and the cast of over 30 “genre-chaotic” virtuosic musicians including Ria Modak, Sarathy Korwar, Jay Chakravorty, Shunya, and Qasim Naqvi. The instrumentation never distracts, though. It’s not showy, and all emulsifies around Sheherazaad’s vocals in a shawl that feels equal parts comforting and oppressive.

Khudgarzi is available now on Bandcamp and most major streaming platforms, including YouTube Music, Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, and Qobuz.

Can a TV be too large? An investigation

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the past couple of years, I’ve wanted to upgrade my home entertainment situation from the humble trappings of my long sufficient 55-inch TCL smart TV to the model much coveted by cinephiles the world over: the OLED.
  • Sources indicate that the organic light-emitting diode is a specific monitor technology that has really changed the TV industry.
